title: Shapes on the Horizon
story:
He walked through the pale, dry grasses. He walked through the long grey shadows cast by the afternoon sun. He walked toward the steady thrum that hummed through the soles of his feet, clutching the cool weight of the metal ring safely in one hand. The Whispering Flats did not feel hostile, but they felt utterly vast—an endless sea of scrub and pale earth that made him realize just how small a creature from the Great Canopy truly was.

There were no branches to catch him here. There were no broad leaves to hide under. There were only open skies and the persistent, ticking rhythm of something enormous hidden miles ahead. When the ground rose into a solitary mound of cracked stone, James climbed it without hesitation, seeking the familiar comfort of height.

From the top of the mound, James looked out across the shimmering heat of the plain. The thin wisp of smoke he had noticed days ago from the safety of his hillside boulder was no longer just a solitary thread. Now, beneath it, sharp and deliberate silhouettes cut into the horizon. They were not trees, for trees curved and swayed with the wind. These shapes were stubbornly straight, forming sharp angles, slanted rooftops, and a towering metal cylinder that puffed deliberate rings of white smoke into the pale sky.

It was a place made of corners. It was a place built with intention. James sat on the warm rock, resting his chin on his knees as the distant, rhythmic clanking drifted faintly over the grass, carrying with it the unmistakable truth that someone out there had built a world entirely unlike the trees.
location: A rocky mound within the Whispering Flats
